story_type: runaway boat with no one aboard
hook: Nobody was driving this boat, and it would not stop
narration: Nobody was driving this boat, and it would not stop circling.
Its driver was in the water.
Crews off Miami found it still running.
A new rule, eleven days old, says small boats need a cut-off switch on a lanyard.
outcome: Crews stopped it by tangling the prop. A good Samaritan pulled the man out.
title: Runaway boat circling with no one aboard
question_comment: Do you clip on the kill switch lanyard every time you drive a boat?

extra_sources.excerpt: MIAMI — A good Samaritan rescued a man in the water in the vicinity of Fisherman's Channel, Monday, at approximately 6 p.m., after he was separated from his vessel. Coast Guard Station Miami Beach and Miami-Dade Fire Rescue crews arrived to the scene with the vessel still running and stopped it by entangling the prop. "As of April 1, vessels 26-feet and under are required to have an engine cut-off switch, and operators are required to wear the lanyard to stop accidents such as this one," said Petty Officer First Class Andrew Sanchez, command duty officer, Sector Miami. "The operator is fortunate the situation was not worse."

description:
On April 12, 2021, a man was separated from his boat near Fisherman's Channel off Miami and a good Samaritan pulled him from the water. Coast Guard Station Miami Beach and Miami-Dade Fire Rescue crews found the boat still running and stopped it by entangling its propeller.
